summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis on chronic steroids was admitted after experiencing hypotension, visual hallucinations, and acute kidney injury at home, one day after receiving his first rituximab infusion. He was found to have an adrenal crisis, likely triggered by the physiological stress of the new biologic therapy. He received intravenous hydrocortisone and fluids in the emergency department with rapid improvement in blood pressure and mental status. His renal function normalized within 24 hours. Nortriptyline was discontinued due to its potential to worsen hallucinations and orthostatic hypotension. His home medications, including dexamethasone and insulin, were continued, and antihypertensives were restarted prior to discharge. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans to coordinate stress-dose steroid coverage and possible observation for future rituximab infusions with his specialists.
